title: London System
intro: d4, Nf3 and Bf4, then e3, c3 and Nbd2: one calm, solid set-up for White against almost anything.

lessons.title: The London set-up
lessons.summary: Bishop out first, then a rock-solid pawn triangle.

steps.text: The London System puts the dark-squared bishop on f4 early, before e3 locks it in. Then White builds a solid triangle of pawns on c3, d4 and e3.
Play the London: d4, Nf3, then the bishop to f4.
steps.hint: Queen's pawn, king's knight, then the bishop goes out before e3.
steps.ifWrong: The London goes d4, Nf3, Bf4.
steps.ifRight: The bishop is out before the pawns close it in.

steps.text: Support d4 and open a path for your other bishop.
steps.hint: A one-square pawn move in front of the king.
steps.ifRight: d4 is supported and the f1 bishop can come out.

steps.text: Black adds pressure on d4 with 4...Nc6.
Develop the queen's knight to d2, where it does not block the c-pawn.
steps.hint: On c3 the knight would stop your c-pawn moving.
steps.ifWrong: In the London the knight goes to d2, keeping c3 free for a pawn.
The triangle needs a pawn on c3.
steps.ifRight: c3, d4, e3: the London fortress. Next come Bd3 and castling.

steps.text: Black offers to trade bishops with ...Bd6. London players usually keep their bishop. Where does it go?
steps.hint: Step back along the diagonal, still eyeing Black's queenside.
steps.ifWrong: Keep the bishop by stepping back to g3.
steps.ifRight: The bishop stays, and if Black takes on g3, your h-pawn takes back.

feedback.f4d6: Trading is fine too. Most London players keep the bishop with Bg3.

lessons.title: Outposts and attacks
lessons.summary: Use the e5 outpost, the open h-file, and the d3 bishop.

steps.text: The London set-up is ready: the pawn triangle stands firm, and both bishops aim at the kingside. Two main plans give White strong play.
Plan one: if Black trades on g3, do not fear doubled pawns. Taking back with the h-pawn opens the h-file for your rook.
Recapture on g3 to open the h-file.
steps.hint: Take with the edge pawn, not the f-pawn.
steps.ifWrong: Play hxg3 so your h1 rook gets an open file against Black's king.
steps.ifRight: The h-file is open, and your rook already eyes h7.

feedback.f2g3: Taking with the f-pawn leaves e3 weak and keeps your rook shut in. Play hxg3.

steps.text: Plan two: plant a knight on e5. Supported by d4 and f4, it dominates the centre and clears the way for Qf3 or f4.
Place your knight on the e5 outpost.
steps.hint: Jump into the centre with the f3 knight.
steps.ifWrong: Play Ne5 to claim the key London outpost.
steps.ifRight: If Black trades knights, dxe5 gains space and drives away the f6 defender.

feedback.e1g1: Castling is good too, but Ne5 seizes the key outpost right away.

steps.text: Black trades off the outpost knight.
Take back on e5 to drive away Black's defender and gain space.
steps.hint: Recapture with the pawn, attacking the knight on f6.
steps.ifWrong: Take with dxe5: the knight on f6 is kicked away and h7 loses its main guard.
steps.ifRight: With the f6 knight forced back, White can build a direct attack on the kingside.

feedback.f4e5: Bxe5 is solid, yet dxe5 kicks the f6 knight away from defending the king.
